sentences.text: The premise holds only on its narrowest reading. The year-over-year test passes, but the same quarter sits 0.2 percentage points below where it was 8 quarters ago, so what reads as expansion is mostly a return to an earlier level.

The comparison base is depressed. The prior year carried the $4.5 billion H20 charge and the shift from Hopper systems to Blackwell, which is why fiscal 2026 fell to 71.1% from 75.0% and why the full-year corollary fails.
Sequentially the filing itself calls gross margin approximately flat, and a quarter-over-quarter gain of 0.04 points is not evidence of a rising trend.

For the decision, the step from this claim to staying overweight assumes margin adds upside into the next report. The record instead shows a plateau at about 75.0%, so further earnings growth would have to come from revenue, which grew +105.9%, rather than from margin.
Even the year-over-year reading is thin. Its room is 1.27x a typical move, and the test held in only 12 of 20 past readings.

Inventory now stands at 119.3 days of cost of revenue against 105.6 a year before, and the last large margin drop came from an inventory charge. The record cannot say whether the current build carries similar risk.

conditions.text: Quarterly gross margin falling below the prior-year level of 72.4% would make the year-over-year test fail.
Quarterly gross margin rising above the two-year high of 75.1% would show expansion beyond recovery rather than a plateau.
An 8-K disclosing an accounting matter, such as a charge tied to inventory, would point to the kind of event that cut margin in the prior year.
